## Recommendation and the actual witness

Search for **spectator-nonraising subloop identities** in a fixed ordinary-source
window. Keep every source row and cancel the unwanted *collected endpoint
coefficients*, rather than dropping rows that individually contain unwanted
terms. This changes the feasible target-isolating identities, not merely the
order in which an equivalent basis is processed. Preserve the saved integral
order, all pinches, exceptional guards, and the original-source proof.

## Three distinct constraints

For a source combination `C_s(n)=Σ_i w_i(n) A_{i,s}(n)` and protected axes J:

| Objective | Endpoint restriction | What it permits |
|---|---|---|
| Exact spectator preservation | `C_s=0` if any `s_j≠0` | No spectator shifts |
| Spectator no-raising | `C_s=0` if any `s_j>0` | Spectator lowering and pinches |
| Global excess nonincrease | `C_s=0` wherever `E(n+s)>E(n)` | Only a globally bounded excess envelope, if established throughout the reached program |

No-raising is **weaker**, not stronger, than exact preservation. On a negative
index, a positive physical shift reduces numerator rank; forbidding it is
still a user-selected physical-index condition, not a general rank-reduction
criterion. Restrict this nomination to the explicitly listed active spectators.
Nor does spectator no-raising prevent dot or rank growth on unprotected axes.

Polynomial vector tangency `V(D_j)=h_j D_j` is a sufficient *source-level*
construction avoiding an increase of that denominator power. It is not the
same as requiring every resulting spectator shift to be zero, nor the same
as cancellation among translated source endpoints. The proposed endpoint
test has a direct finite-column authority boundary and does not claim to
compute a complete logarithmic-derivation module.

## What the primary literature actually offers

**Forcer:** §§3.1–3.2 seek simultaneous dot/numerator lowering, then separate
boundary equations when a dot reaches1 or a numerator0. They eliminate
unwanted high-complexity terms from small translated equation sets and combine
opposing recurrences; repeated self-composition can instead inflate terms and
coefficients. This supports a constrained local elimination objective, not
unconditional whole-frontier expansion. The published triangle formula has a
massless connecting line; the diamond's lower and spectator lines must be
massless. Neither formula applies verbatim to this fully massive triangle.
[Forcer §§3.1–3.2](https://arxiv.org/html/1704.06650v1),
[diamond rule §§1–2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1504.08258).

**Smith–Zeng:** §2.3 imposes polynomial tangency on a chosen denominator set.
§3.1 distinguishes operator-level coefficient elimination from the final
small, partially symbolic neighborhood solves. Their sector definition fixes
positive powers, not only support; most indices left symbolic are numerator
indices. Consequently a successful fixed-dot rule is not automatically a rule
for arbitrary positive spectator powers. The relevant transfer is to search
only the still-unresolved boundary and retain exact lower-sector tails, not
restart unconstrained Laporta everywhere. A failed finite neighborhood here
must remain a bank/window negative, not a declaration of a new master.
[Primary paper §§2.3,3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.11140v2).

The2026 LoopIn follow-up explicitly builds polynomial-vector identities as
combinations of differently seeded ordinary IBPs, performs coefficient-level
elimination, and subsequently solves missing rules near unresolved indices.
Its §4 warns that fewer equations are denser and rational reconstruction can
remain the bottleneck. This is compatible with our source-span architecture,
not evidence that a smaller source count or this five-loop campaign must win.
[LoopIn §§2,3.1,4](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19909v1).

**Module intersection:** the Baikov constraints
`Σ a_i ∂_i P + bP=0` and `a_i=z_i b_i` separately avoid dimension shifts and
selected doubled denominators; intersecting their polynomial modules combines
the properties. The generators are then multiplied by monomials to supply
target relations. A cut computation loses off-cut information unless all tails
are reconstructed. A field nullspace is not a polynomial-module syzygy basis,
and the module construction is not itself a favourable-descendant certificate.
[Böhm et al., §§2.1–2.2,3](https://arxiv.org/html/1805.01873v2).

**TIDE:** the actual fully massive thesis §8.1.2 uses rank-preserving and
dot-preserving combinations only at the corresponding generated boundaries;
ordinary IBPs are often sparser elsewhere. Its larger generated halo is
explicitly distinct from the requested region, and the protected sources do
not generally eliminate the need for that halo. This is evidence against
globally replacing the ordinary generator just because a constrained class
works locally. It concerns bounded integer/one-symbolic-exponent systems,
not complete all-index rule closure. We inspected the primary thesis and
existing repository census, not an unavailable TIDE source implementation.
[Luthe thesis, pp.88–89](https://noah.nrw/ubbihs/download/pdf/5131192),
[repository comparison](tide_five_loop_census.md#6-tides-reduction-algorithm-and-what-transfers).

## Existing algebra and the genuinely missing adapter

API audit precedes any proposed arithmetic. Cargo pins Symbolica3.0.0 from
vendor commit `ef0db494533c87adb40356c996241680dc5a7bff`; current public Rust
documentation is3.0.1, not a reason to upgrade. Public native services include
`SparseRowReducer::{new,add_row,u,pivots,back_substitute}`, dense
`Matrix::{solve_any,row_reduce}`, and polynomial coefficient grouping.
[Current native sparse API](https://docs.rs/symbolica/latest/symbolica/tensors/sparse/struct.SparseRowReducer.html),
[current matrix documentation](https://symbolica.io/docs/matrices.html).
Pinned source was checked in `vendor/symbolica/lib/numerica/src/tensors/`
and `vendor/symbolica/src/poly/`. Ideal `GroebnerBasis::new` exists; this audit
found no public general polynomial-module syzygy/intersection service there.
That is a qualified API finding, not a mathematical impossibility claim.

RustRed already provides the important operations:

- `logarithmic_kernel/linear.rs` uses native sparse field elimination on an
  identity-augmented matrix, then replays the kernel. A bounded polynomial
  ansatz can use native coefficient grouping; no custom elimination is needed.
- `identity/tangent/construction.rs` provides a narrower prescribed
  two-denominator tangent construction. It is not a complete arbitrary
  spectator-module solver.
- `symbolic_projector/source.rs`, `project.rs` and the native source prover
  already carry original ordinary contributions, translate coefficients with
  shifts, compose the full image, and retain poles/guards.
- `foundry/completion/spired/source_basis/compile.rs` computes the complete
  sector/order-local ordinary-source RREF with forward and reverse span checks.
  It deliberately does not prune against the target or chart. Vendored
  SpIReD `solver.tpp::rowReduce` similarly eliminates by leading terms. An
  invertible rebasis with fixed column order cannot produce a different RREF.

The recently successful endpoint-locality experiment changes this last
objective: raw25 target isolation produced nonlocal15/10-tail rules; adding
full-image spectator constraints recovered both independently proved
seven-tail banana charts from25 unweighted ordinary rows. Chart, offset and
protected axes were supplied; eight weights were not. This is a demonstrated
selection mechanism, not automatic family recognition. See
[the source nomination and exact evidence](banana_moment_nomination_2026-10-04.md).

Existing explicit `forbidden_shifts` would suffice if the complete post-fixed
source-image universe were available to the caller. Current inspection
reports do not expose that universe, and the parser rejects shifts outside it.
Therefore the smallest generic adapter is now authorized:
`forbid_endpoint_increases_on_axes`, deriving `s_j>0` constraints from that
actual universe before row selection. It unions all existing mandatory F,
permits cancellation between rows, and rechecks the exact full composed image.
The companion `forbid_endpoint_changes_on_axes` remains unchanged.
Absent/empty options preserve the old path. No engine, coefficient algebra,
module kernel, ordering, or closure policy changes. All117 optimized research
tests pass (seven new); the binary links to the same cached0257 core/app
libraries. Evidence: `TMP/rule-optimizer-20261003/candidates/endpoint-no-raising-build-v1/`.
At that stage no owner31 native result existed; subsequent results are recorded below.

## Smallest exact falsifier and the campaign gate

1. Obtain node2975's actual selected rule, full source cell, native nonzero
   image and immutable family/order/root binding from the already planned
   diagnostic. Do not infer them from a CP6 edge list.
2. Preregister **one** ordinary-source window informed by that target/chart,
   all selected original rows, no supplied solution weights, and no automatic
   refinement. Compare the same bank/offset/order with and without no-raising
   on `[0,1,4,6,9,13]`. Keep free axes justified by the chart; a singleton
   coefficient solution alone is not a reusable parametric rule.
3. Require native whole-chart original-source replay, target isolation,
   retained raw/normalization poles, root admissibility, strict saved-order
   descent, and all boundary cells. A unit triangle-power face and every
   pinch stay explicit. The banana `a=b=1` gap remains unresolved: its two
   known windows lose their target coefficient there. The new predicate does
   not repair that absence by itself.
4. Record all tails, support/rank/power changes, guard fragments and exact
   applicability at the witness. A finite-span miss stops that window;
   first-candidate proof refusal rejects only that candidate. Neither is
   global nonexistence. A valid rule reproducing the existing boundary is
   also a useful negative. No automatic degree, bank or cap growth.
5. A changed **complete** native boundary with a concrete reason to expect
   fewer downstream obligations—including easier pinches, not just fewer
   tails—may justify a scoped matched whole-workload comparison with unchanged
   baseline fallback, terminals and cold checks. Shared descendants,
   pinches/routing and coefficient cost decide the outcome. Neither330→fewer
   tails nor a larger local boundary establishes that outcome or authorizes a
   second campaign by itself.

The primary mechanism is fewer reachable obligations from a different valid
identity. It is not a target-order hack: order and descent remain fixed, and
no hard endpoint is silently declared lower or discarded.

## Deferred stronger objective: an explicit global excess envelope

Let `E(n)=Σ max(n_i−1,0)+Σ max(−n_i,0)`. On a fixed support, it is a linear
dot-plus-rank cost; across pinches it is piecewise linear. Requiring
`E(n+s)≤E(n)` for every admitted nonzero tail, including pinches, is a different
global objective; neither it nor spectator no-raising implies the other in
general. An eventual complete-chart
predicate should use existing native sign-cell/degree geometry, not an
unproved linearization across support changes or a new polyhedral engine.

The current
`crates/rustred-core/src/foundry/artifact/source_port/total_excess.rs`
already constructs sector-dependent finite envelopes: same-support excess
does not increase, while pinch jumps use a shift-norm/support-loss bound.
The new objective would remove those jumps. Together with authenticated
nonincreasing native routing, it could provide one explicit finite physical
envelope **only if the property holds throughout the reached program**.
One improved owner or selected rule is insufficient; independently enqueued
unbounded helper domains also defeat the premise. This is not the first
conditional termination argument: finite concrete seeds, finite branching
and well-founded support/owner descent already provide one. A uniform E bound
would be quantitative and might prevent abstract widening, but its cardinality
can still be enormous. Prior bounded-helper negatives remain in force.
Reopen only on an actual offending pinch with an exactly proved replacement;
no global clipping, new scheduler or envelope implementation is proposed now.

## Negatives that this proposal does not erase

The earlier all-active tangent module produced zero images in one ansatz;
selective protection lacked a target in another, and tangent priority worsened
the four-loop closure. The48-row/144-weight boundary-polynomial template
searches also missed. These are documented in
[protected sources](profile_guided_protected_sources_2026-10-03.md) and
[boundary-preserving search](boundary_preserving_rule_search_2026-10-04.md).
The changed objective is a specifically nominated endpoint condition, not a
renaming of those negative searches or evidence of module completeness.

The direct owner0 quadratic-D13 Baikov recurrence remains a structural
**NO-GO** in its proposed chart. Only G45/G54 contain D13, giving
`[D13²]det(G)=−det(G123)/4`. That minor contains
`+(D3+1)(D14+D4−D7−D10)²/16`, including inactive-only numerator monomials
which preserve the target's active powers and D13 rank but increase its other
numerator rank. They cannot be divided out as scalar coefficients, and the
lower-D13 terms cannot cancel those columns. A zero ISP exponent does not set
the integrated D variable to zero. This hand-derived, independently checked
obstruction is not a native checker receipt and does not exclude combinations
eliminating the minor. See the
[actual-coordinate derivation](structural_recurrence_alternatives_2026-10-04.md).

The larger alternative is a targeted polynomial-module intersection or a
small coupled operator block retaining lower-sector tails, not an unrestricted
full-Laporta replacement. It needs a demonstrated failure of the bounded
ordinary-source objective, a budgeted Symbolica-backed API path, and evidence
that its denser relations reduce shared work. Those prerequisites are absent;
it is deferred rather than sold as the next implementation.

## Next design, not a run: eliminate a costly routed boundary class

The banana results separate three objectives: few source weights, few RHS
terms, and little downstream work. None implies the others. The four-source
rule has10 tails and opens D3/D4; preserving the original numerator directions
recovers eight sources and7 tails. Its additionally allowed spectator-lowering
columns are not selected. Thus the current first-target projector is a
**feasibility selector**, not an optimizer of pinches, support sparsity or
shared descendants. Adding a permitted endpoint does not require its use.

For a fixed full source image matrix A and a prospectively chosen costly
endpoint class B, the existing exact operation is simply
`w A[:,B]=0`, with a nonzero target coefficient. Native coefficient cancellation
acts on the whole combination. The same target order and final strict
descent proof apply. This changes the admissible boundary, unlike merely
rebasing A. It can trade a costly numerator/routing branch for several easier
pinches without assigning a small cost to every pinch automatically.

This is not a new algebraic idea: Forcer's elimination of unwanted operator
terms and TIDE's wanted/unwanted boundary separation are relevant precedents
already cited above. It also uses the same F-column mechanism as our earlier
negative local-cut experiments. The prospective difference is **which complete
boundary class is excluded and why**, supported by exact weighted transport,
not a claim that a newly named constraint defeats the prior shared-work
negatives.

### One preregistered owner31 falsifier, after generic-chart inspection

1. Use the complete native selected-rule event and source cell for node2975,
   and the evaluator's independently reviewed weighted-route output. Retain
   nonrouted children, all pinches, coefficients, caps, guards and source
   provenance. Per-term numerator expansion is not the final weighted sum;
   a cancelled route term is not a remaining obligation. An interrupted
   global fallback window cannot establish an endpoint's exclusive cone.
2. Choose **one** endpoint class by a fixed, pre-search criterion: the largest
   retained exact routed-image class in that complete observation, with a
   deterministic native owner/route-signature tie-break. If there is no
   materially large surviving class, or the diagnostic is incomplete, park
   this witness. Grouping/cost is nomination metadata, never algebraic proof.
3. Bind one translated ordinary-source window to the actual saved rule's
   authenticated target/recentering information, rather than guessing an
   offset from CP6. Declare the bank, whole chart, limits and all columns to
   exclude before solving. Include the costly class's contributing original
   endpoint columns, even if several feed the same routed image. This is a
   sufficient and possibly overrestrictive ban; it cannot exploit all
   cancellations that occur only after routing. Require at least one genuinely
   retained incumbent column to be banned, so the unchanged incumbent cannot
   satisfy the proposed objective.
   The observation nominates columns at this singleton, not the full generic
   preimage of a routed class: distinct affine maps can coincide here, and
   other candidate columns may reach the same class. Without complete generic
   preimage accounting, claim only the declared column exclusion and measure
   the full weighted boundary again at the nominated point.
4. Perform at most one exact projection in that bank with the class forbidden
   and other admissible tails—including spectator lowering—allowed. Existing
   `forbidden_shifts` suffices when the specified columns are in its full
   post-fixed universe. If the actual source/window or column membership
   cannot be established from existing services, stop preparation rather than
   silently drop columns or grow the bank. Whole-chart replay and all native
   proof obligations remain mandatory. A miss/refusal is confined to this
   bank/objective, never global IBP incompleteness.
5. A proved result must be evaluated by its **complete coefficient-weighted
   routed boundary**, not just disappearance of B or reduced RHS count. New
   costly routes can replace the removed ones. Even fewer exact routed keys
   do not establish fewer whole-program descendants; only a fixed bounded
   cohort comparison with unchanged fallback/terminals and full closure can
   justify consideration of another campaign. No export or such comparison
   is authorized by this design note.

No new syzygy service is needed for that finite-span experiment. What is not
currently provided is a soft optimizer over guarded source-kernel solutions,
or an exact objective for their globally shared routed descendants. A sum of
local column costs is only a heuristic: nonzero-support selection, rational
coefficient complexity, transport cancellation, conditional guards and shared
reachability make the actual objective nonadditive. A future implementation
would need independently valid complete alternatives and an explicit cost
model, not a custom polynomial kernel. Full module intersection becomes
relevant only if a specifically justified family of polynomially weighted
operators lies outside the frozen ordinary window; finite failure alone is
not evidence that this larger operation will help.

## Liu–Mitov: useful allowed-boundary design, not a missing solver

**Primary-source précis.** Liu–Mitov construct single-index scalar/matrix
recurrences, then a triangular alternative. Their coefficient search eliminates
unwanted integral columns while retaining a target; shifted ordinary IBPs
supply the rows. The triangular RHS lowers numerator weight, or moves within
a layer toward a chosen index hierarchy; lower-sector terms have additional
weight restrictions. Their presentation largely fixes positive indices and
omits doubled propagators, with separate base-integral treatment. Finite-basis
existence does not establish every restricted triangular ansatz; the stated
shift-depth stopping heuristic is empirical. Matrix recurrences can swell
rational coefficients. Benchmarks are one-/two-loop examples; coefficient
evaluation dominates their triangular finite-field timings, and end-to-end
comparisons are not uniformly favorable. See
[§§II.1–II.5, III.1–III.3 and IV](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.05923v1).

**Repository comparison/inference.** Section III.2's forbidden-column/target
test is already the operation in
`tools/research/rule_optimizer/symbolic_projector/project.rs:343`: native
Symbolica `SparseRowReducer`, a target pivot, identity-augmented source weights
and complete image replay. The public API audit above supplies everything
needed for a finite-window test; neither a new module kernel nor a new solver
named after this paper is justified. An invertible source rebasis with the
same complete rows, columns and target cannot change exact feasibility.
Changing the *allowed RHS* can, as our locality tests demonstrate. A different
first candidate is still not evidence of an optimized boundary.

Our existing native rules already descend in their saved order. Importing a
different index hierarchy without rebuilding and proving a coherent program
would be an order change, not this experiment. Abstract containment SCCs are
also not cyclic concrete recurrences: the sealed-SCC verifier already accepts
their coverage, and the Q1707/A2738 local incoming demands were circular.
An algebraic triangular identity neither repairs that demand provenance nor
justifies clipping a broader lender. The relevant mechanism is a different
complete recurrence boundary with less downstream work, not another DAG claim.

### A distinct but presently gated pinch objective

Node2975 has physical numerator rank0 and large positive powers. A demand
that loses at least one rank unit for every support loss would exclude every
nonzero pinch there. It is not a suitable default transfer of the paper's
specialized numerator ansatz. Instead, a prospective sufficient objective is
`R(n+s) <= R(n)` for **all** retained tails, including lower-support tails,
while retaining the present saved order. At this witness it allows scalar
pinches with rank0 and excludes actual numerator-producing pinches; it does
not demand negative rank. This differs from selected-spectator no-raising and
from global dot-plus-rank E nonincrease.

The smallest useful discriminator remains gated on the evaluator's complete
selected-rule/source-cell/weighted-boundary observation. First establish an
actual surviving costly rank-increasing pinch. If none exists, this objective
does not distinguish the incumbent and should be parked. If one exists,
preregister one already justified original-source window and a complete
forbidden set for that objective, with no source/degree/order refinement.
The existing `forbidden_shifts` accepts an explicit complete set from the
actual post-fixed universe. For a rank-zero chart, strict preservation of all
initially zero indices is an available stronger sufficient restriction **only

(n_j−1) I(n) = (5d/2−Σ n_i+1) I(n−e_j)

### Relation to lower-sector freedom in the literature

Bree et al. explicitly identify freedom between forms equivalent under their
maximal-cut ordering but differing in lower-sector terms; optimizing those
couplings remains unimplemented in that work. This motivates investigating
boundary changes, not assuming an available optimization theorem.
[Section6](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15381v1#S6).

The unequal-mass banana example uses a master-basis-dependent projection that
changes tadpole couplings in its differential equations. Tadpoles remain
separate master integrals; projection is not a physical proof that they vanish.
Our full-image source proof cannot import that quotient as permission to drop
pinches. [Section3.5](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.23594v1#S3.SS5).

Critical-syzygy construction combines generators and imposes linear vanishing
constraints on out-of-power-counting monomials. Its cut-based completeness
argument is modulo pinch integrals, with pinch topologies handled separately.
[Sections3.4 and5.1.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.17681v1#S5.SS1.SSS2).
Our smaller diagnostic instead keeps the full original-family weighted image,
all pinches and native proof conditions, while preserving the leading recurrence.
Relaxing column identity to a rank cap tests one chosen boundary objective;
it neither implements those full algorithms nor establishes campaign benefit.

### A separate collective-correction hypothesis, not a magic-relation claim

Crisanti et al. distinguish cancellation of all generating-sector terms from
the additional independence from relations generated within subsectors. Their
critical-variety equivalence is conjectural; the syzygy argument uses stated
assumptions, including a gcd condition. Our possible next test is different
and elementary: take the kernel of the unpinched columns of the existing291
ordinary rows, then seek a collective lower-sector correction preserving B0's
leading recurrence while cancelling P9. Unlike the earlier strict291 search,
this does not demand removal of every rank-one column. This is our inference,
not an implementation of their algorithm or evidence of a magic relation;
independence, full-image proof and useful downstream work would remain open.
No critical-variety calculation or collective-kernel experiment was run.
[Sections3.1,4.4 and6, v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.29789).

### Transverse geometry check: no additional probe or new authority

The transverse-integration paper motivates projection orthogonal to a subloop's
external momenta; its general construction involves inverse Gram matrices and
may map into different families. This is background, not evidence for our
five-loop correction. [Sections4.1–4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.04783v2#S4.SS1).

After D7 is pinched, write k=k1, q=k2-k4 and p=k3. The k-dependent proper
denominators are X=D1=k²-1 and Y=D14=(k+q)²-1. Here q²=D10+1 is an integrated
variable, so dividing by q² would introduce an internal massless denominator,
not an external scalar coefficient. Equal-mass reflection exchanges the X/Y
powers and does not preserve this chart's arbitrary a and fixed1.

Our denominator-cleared polynomial check instead uses
`V=((k+q)·q)p-((k+q)·p)q`. Direct differentiation gives div_k V=0,
V·(k+q)=0 and V·k=T=q²(k·p)-(q·p)(k·q). Thus the integrated ordinary IBP for
`X^(-(a-1))*Y^(-1)`, with k-independent spectators, is
`-2(a-1) integral[T*X^(-a)*Y^(-1)]=0`; it is not a pointwise integrand identity.
In the actual family,

`4T = 2(D10+1)(D1+D3-D6+1) - (D2-D4-D9+D15)(D14-D1-D10-1)`.

D4 opens a new numerator direction, while D10 can pinch. D3 and D6 have
opposite coefficients. For the corresponding common carrier this would pair
to zero against an equal-entry two-column witness; equality of displayed λ
strings remains explanatory only, and native exact pairing is the authority.
The independently checked hand derivation therefore does not establish a new
obstruction breaker or a cheaper recurrence. No transverse source was added,
proved or benchmarked. This is distinct from the earlier isolated-owner2
factorization discussion and does not evade the actual-family restrictions.

The next conceptual candidate is an **exit-complete chart bundle**: a finite
collection of guarded rules whose every concrete image stays in another
covered chart or reaches an independently justified exit. Existing concrete
descent checks compose through support cardinality, Route/Apply phase and the
owner-local well-order. They can justify induction once all transfer and
boundary premises hold. They do not rank symbolic containment/hull edges or
make unresolved lower sectors free. The previously rejected334-node SCC
omitted independent incoming demands; invoking induction does not fix that.
See the existing [concrete finiteness discussion](demand_directed_symbolic_sccs_2026-10-04.md).

One possible representation partitions an authenticated resource envelope by
saved applicability cases and retains transfers between those cases, rather
than creating a new node for every translated demand box. The single-family
`total_excess.rs` audit already supplies part of this machinery, under its
ordering and census assumptions. The missing study is routed multi-owner
integration with rule priority, sign/guard faces and complete side exits.
Case count does not guarantee graph size: intersections may fragment badly,
and a broad envelope may encounter genuine uncovered cases. First falsify
that representation on a completed control; do not promise a shortcut to
five-loop closure or start a new proof-system implementation from this note.
Furthermore, `AfterBaselinePartitionWholePiece` activation depends on the
baseline query piece. A quotient keyed only by owner/batch/rule IDs would lose
that context; preserve it explicitly or begin with ordinary Partition rules.

Primary program-analysis literature supports composing paths before joins and
checking inductive transfer relations, not importing an IBP solver or ignoring
weighted tails. [Monniaux–Gonnord](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1106.2637) motivate
path-focused fixed-point analysis; [Monniaux](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.4844)
distinguishes whole-block abstraction from composing per-step abstractions.
[Frohn](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2001.01516) treats guarded single-path integer
acceleration, whose premises do not automatically cover branching IBPs.
Our proposed transfer is a research inference. No custom CAS, polyhedral
kernel or blanket loop-acceleration claim follows.

The completed first diagnostic is the existing full-parent applied observer:

recurrence depths must not be compared by raw endpoint counts. Also, native
UniformNonzero Apply images already preserve their A/R/D geometry exactly.
An actual precision-loss diagnosis must involve demonstrated Route/publication
overcoverage, not a generic complaint about boxes.

### A more discriminating algebraic objective

The old rule14 and fresh rule0 share exactly the same six equal-E, same-support
transfers `+e_j−e_D12`, for `j∈{D1,D2,D5,D7,D9,D10}`. Each acts over all19
original inputs with identical source and target geometry:114 point-pairs in
each program. This is not an assertion of coefficient equality. The previous
D11 cancellation did not remove any of these redistributions.

This motivates **degree-plateau elimination**: combine original IBPs so that a
target bypasses a set of same-degree transfers and exits to lower degree or
lower support. RustRed's current cofinal policy is weaker: it accepts equal-E
terms that descend under the remaining degree/coordinate tie-breaks. The
algebraic objective therefore changes, without changing the source identities,
their exact replay, or the CAS.

The smallest registered falsifier uses the same125-source bank at all19 exact
points, removes D11-only preservation, and forbids the six known-present columns.
Full-output checks must detect any newly introduced equal/higher-E same-support
terms. A successful six-column cancellation is **not** necessarily a strict-E
rule; a miss is only a finite-bank negative. Pinches, zero-sector provenance,
all original guards and numerical terminals remain explicit. No large halo
enumeration, new kernel, arbitrary terminal declaration or production launch is
licensed by this experiment.

The experiment completed in39.548s: **all19 cases miss** after125 rows and19
native descent refinements each. No algebra/resource/observer refusal occurred
and every owned process drained. Evidence:
`profiles/production-rule14-exact19-plateau-v1/`, execution`fb0ee5bf…1ca6b93`.
This is a negative for the frozen restoration-path source span with its final
accumulated forbidden columns and unchanged native ordering. It is not global
strict-E infeasibility. An alternative pivot within that complete span cannot
create a missing relation; additional original-source directions or a genuinely
different admissibility objective need separate justification. No parametric
rule or performance comparison was produced by this test.

The19 exclusions are identical at all19 points. Seventeen introduce a
same-support numerator with ΔR=ΔE=+1 and ΔA=0. The other two are equal-E dot
transfers `+D14−D12` and `+D15−D12`, disallowed by the coordinate tie-break.
The obstruction is therefore mostly genuine degree growth, not merely an
unfortunate tie-break. The next bounded diagnostic freezes point00's final F
and asks the existing exact dual/preimage service which additional original
sources can break that particular obstruction. A nonzero witness pairing would
nominate sources, not prove a useful rule or a smaller final boundary.

Existing machinery already supplies much of a prospective block method:
`SectorSolver::solve_numeric_cases` shares one GPLU system across finite targets;
the source projector composes exact weights back to original rows; and the
native reducer coalesces weighted terms. The concrete routed campaign, however,
drops coefficients after each local application and follows all remaining keys.
Whole-block cancellation *before* that publication could avoid intermediate
obligations; merely adding another linear solver would not. Any chart-level
composition must use shifted coefficients `c(n) d(n+s)`, shifted guards and
actual route maps. All uncancelled external columns remain obligations.

### Literature implications, not imported performance claims

[SAILIR, §§III.5–6 and AppendixD](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05034) searches
over weighted expressions and short reduction episodes, rather than choosing
each rewrite only from its target. Its finite-field two-loop study motivates
looking at cancellation across multiple substitutions. It does not establish
exact all-parameter guards, five-loop performance, or unconditional termination
of a heuristic search. For RustRed, a small heuristic episode proposer followed
by existing exact original-source replay is a more proportionate first test
than training a topology-specific model. This is a proposed transfer, not an
implemented SAILIR port.

Independent review rejects a beam restricted to the same125-row span and
accumulated F: flexible row selection cannot reverse its complete exact miss.
The prospective useful role is choosing a better feasible expression boundary
or nominating genuinely new source rows, then exact replay. The existing public
modular nomination interface returns source support, not an expression-state
beam; that extension is deferred rather than described as already available.

[Kira3, §3.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.20197v1) supports target-directed
equation selection through finite-field elimination. RustRed already has a
related dependency-trace mechanism; another sparse solver is not the missing
piece. [Blade, §3](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.14621v2) provides block-triangular
reduction methods but uses numerical reductions to a master basis as input.
That prerequisite prevents treating it as a ready certificate for our unknown
five-loop boundary. Neither paper supplies a practical universal source-depth
bound for this campaign.

[FIRE7, §§2.6 and3.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07150) provides an important
counterweight: its linear-combination workflow principally reduces the amount
of coefficient reconstruction, not necessarily the individual reductions
needed underneath. Its symbolic presolve combines relations without shifted
operator application. Neither feature alone proves a smaller RustRed dependency
graph. The needed evidence remains cancellation of a complete, weighted boundary
and then a cheaper completed cohort in the unchanged shared-owner context.

The current experiment and research do not justify a second production
campaign. They specifically replace an unproductive one-direction objective
with a test of joint algebraic progress; ordinary campaign optimization and
unproved terminal inflation are not being substituted for that test.

### Next implementation: collect a complete short plateau cut

The complementary experiment changes what is propagated, not the source bank.
For each fixed input independently, compose its saved rule with one further
application to same-owner, equal-E children. Keep every other child as an
explicit weighted boundary, including pinches and any E increase. A conditional,
unmatched or failed child application retains the whole original child; partial
RHS output must never replace it. At this identical, bounded cut compare the
distinct uncollected boundary with its native exact coefficient sums.

This research-only adapter reuses native rule application and Symbolica
addition/multiplication/zero tests. It does not sum different original input
equations into one, declare new masters, clip lower sectors, or replace the
production traversal. Start with the original90-point four-loop control and
all29 original five-loop parents, not only the19 previously studied points.
Pointwise matching can select different rules from a whole-domain match; the
experiment must say so and retain selected-rule identities. Even substantial
local cancellation would still need a completed shared-context cost comparison
and a reusable source-replayed rule before a production recommendation.

`profiles/plateau-cut-original-controls-depth4-v1/`.

This ends the fixed-policy experiment: **park it rather than tune deeper**.
Local exact cancellation is real, but the shared-boundary effect remains
small and no completed whole-campaign speedup was demonstrated. Different
depths expose different boundaries and cannot be compared as a work reduction.
The opt-in research observer is retained; it is not enabled in the second
campaign requested by the user. That delivery instead uses the separately
validated complementary banana rules and explicitly reports their limited
whole-cohort evidence. There is no claim that the new campaign will close or
outperform the current run.

Depth-two evidence remains under`profiles/plateau-cut-original-controls-v2/`;
the earlier default-off regression is under
`profiles/plateau-cut-original-controls-v1/legacy-default-off/`. The corrected
observer handles redundant singleton cap normalization. The final audit also
retains all off-plateau exits and per-parent sums; it does not sum unrelated
input equations together to manufacture cancellation.
